newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Micron beats estimates but falls.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Micron beats estimates but falls.

text.p: On Monday, options investors were betting on solid earnings from Micron Technology Inc, which they got after the market closed.
What they did not get was an earnings-related rally in the stock, which was down 4-1/2 at 39-5/8 in late trading on consolidated volume of 13.8 million shares.
Traders said no definable trends were evident in the options activity except for the sharp decline in volatilities from the March series out to April and July.
Order flows were strong on both sides, traders said, but options sellers appeared to be outpacing options buyers.
After the market closed Monday, Micron reported fiscal second quarter profit from operations of $0.18 a share, better than the Wall Street estimate of $0.15 a share.
But that was still down 79 percent from the year ago quarter, and Micron's $0.66 per-share earnings included $0.48 of extraordinary gains.
"When they looked at the adjusted numbers, they started smacking" the stock, one options trader said of investors' reaction to the earnings report.
But with the uncertainty of earnings out of the way, volatilities fell sharply across the board.
"We're mostly seeing volatility come in," said Rob Kovell, lead market maker in Micron at the Pacific Exchange. "I can't say we've seen anything one-directional.
"I think a lot of it is closing transactions," he said. "People who protected themselves for the earnings are now taking (their positions) off.
"It's busy on both sides, with no real trends," he added.
The most active Micron option was the March 40 calls, which traded a total of around 11,780 contracts. The March 40 put traded a total of nearly 7,500 contracts.
Micron options trade on the Pacific Exchange and the Chicago Board Options Exchange.
Other busy Micron options included the April 40 calls, the April 45 calls and the April 40 puts.

Jon Najarian, president of Mercury Trading, the designated primary market maker for Micron options at the CBOE, said volatility in the March 40 calls and puts fell to the mid-60 region from around 90 Monday.
He said volatilities of longer-dated options were down sharply as well, with the July at-the-moneys dropping to the mid-50 region, for example.
"Right now they have a pretty good handle on what the downside is," Najarian said, citing the 37 area as a support zone.
"And since we're trading down toward that level, they are very comfortably selling option premium now," he added.
He said all March options expire at the end of this week but Micron options effectively had their expiration today.

"It's safe to say this is expiration for Micron," he said. "The folks out there who are in the Marches are now liquidating. Volatility came down so much because they were selling those out and rolling out to other months."
